ITEM 2.  WRITTEN AND ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Michel Shane was called and confirmed his comments were intended for ltem No.
  4.A.

  Arthur Kelly expressed concern regarding the proposed roundabouts on Pacific
  Coast Highway (PCH) due to narrowing 1.5 miles north and south of the two
  circles, which would make ingress and egress difficult for nearby residences. He
  stated only visible law enforcement officers and the activation of speed cameras
  would slow traffic on PCH. The project was described as a pilot but was intended
  to be in place for two years and provided for additional parking on segments of
  PCH where it was not currently allowed.

  Brian Zein (plus l minute donated by Heba Rosliani) expressed concern regarding
  the proposed roundabouts on PCH and the lack of public information regarding
  the project. Those he spoke to in the neighboring area were unaware of the
  project. and when informed they expressed opposition. His paramount concern
  was potential impacts during a fire as the roundabouts would occur in a primary
  evacuation route. The full schematic of the project had not been provided to the
  public depicting the narrowing of the highway before and after the roundabouts.
  Brian stated one roundabout was close to a fire station and could create difficulty
  for emergency vehicles. He asked for more public information prior to the
  Planning Commission hearing.

  Jo Drummond thanked the Commission for their support in the rebuild
  community and in particular thanked Chair Leonard for his openness, integrity
  and help with the Rebuild Taskforce. She provided an update on the status of her
  rebuild and suggested an evaluation of a protected bike lane in relation to the
  proposed roundabouts.

  Commissioner Mazza announced the City would hold a Zoom meeting regarding
  the proposed roundabouts on October 22. 2025.

  Vice Chair Riddick expressed her appreciation for public input regarding the
  roundabouts and how they were studied. She asked about the City‘s authority
  regarding permitting on a State-owned highway.
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes of October 20, 2025
  Page 3 of 10

  Assistant Community Development Director Eaton confirmed that Public Works
  would host a Zoom meeting and Caltrans staff would also likely be available to
  respond to questions regarding the proposed roundabouts. He noted that the City
  has the authority to issue coastal development permits for Caltrans projects which
  require one ifthe work will occur within City limits.

  Commissioner Kamins thanked Arthur and Brian for their comments and stated
  residents should be provided with more information.

  Chair Leonard noted that much of the City was within 500 feet of the proposed
  Paciflc Coast Highway project area and asked how notifications were handled.

  Recording Secretary Evans noted that for projects with Citywide impact, a legal
  notice was published in the Malibu Times and postcards were sent to interested
  paities, which included a variety ofnotification lists that residents could opt into.

  Vice Chair Riddick thanked Jo Drummond for her reports on the rebuild process.

  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DIRECTOR REPORT

  Assistant Community Development Director Eaton announced the resignation of
  Principal Planner Brooks and thanked her for over seven years of service to the
  City of Malibu. He provided an update on rebuild statistics and upcoming rebuild
  meetings.
